judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate claims-made caption whose terms ('claims-made and reported', 'discovered and reported') are all defined or elaborated elsewhere; nothing in it is genuinely two-sided on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states claims are covered only if reported 'during the policy period', while Insuring Agreements I.A/I.B (c008/c009) and Section VIII (c076) permit reporting during an 'extended reporting period', a mismatch a court could be asked to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short integration listing of the documents making up the policy; its terms are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives no order of precedence among the form, the Declarations and the sixteen endorsements, several of which (Endorsements 5, 8, 10, 11) purport to delete and replace the same provisions, so the reach of this clause could matter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '100 % minimum-earned as of the first day of the Policy Period ... whichever is earlier' is awkward and the OCR is garbled, but the intent (fully earned premium) is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely conflicts with General Condition IX.A.3 (c079), which contemplates remaining 'unearned premium' earned pro rata and refunded within thirty days of cancellation — impossible if 100% is minimum-earned at inception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical all-caps notice repeated in the policy form; the wording is standard and self-explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same tension as c001 with the extended reporting period provisions (c076, c129) which allow post-period reporting of claims deemed made on the last day of the policy period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional signpost saying quoted terms are defined in Section V; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several endorsements add quoted terms ('transportation', 'covered operations', 'non-owned covered locations') and 'covered operations' in Endorsement 6 is never defined anywhere, which slightly undercuts this promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration and reliance recital; the language is conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the Representations condition (c084) and the Fraud exclusion (c059) rather than contradicting anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in conditioning coverage on the Declarations identifying the coverage as underwritten; plain in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations Items 2 and 3 do identify Coverages A and B, and supplemental coverages are added by endorsement, so the lead-in fits, subject only to whether endorsement-added coverages are 'identified on the Declarations'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period' is a demanding and contestable temporal test, and 'arising out of a pollution condition' carries the usual breadth questions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 5 (c120) and Endorsement 10 (c136) each purport to delete this same Subsection A 'in its entirety' and replace it with different text, leaving genuine doubt as to which version governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'commenced, in whole or part, prior to the policy period' is workable, though the OCR typo 'nolicy period' and the whole/part split invite argument about conditions straddling inception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Coverage A (c008), which requires commencement 'in their entirety' during the period, the two together are designed to be complementary but leave the boundary case to be argued; the Divested Property exclusion (c055) expressly carves Coverage B out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and internally consistent attachment mechanics for the self-insured retention; the obligations are stated twice over for clarity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 (c108) sets a separate Catastrophe Management-Specific retention and Endorsement 6 alters what erodes limits, but neither contradicts this attachment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A per-condition limit tied to a Declarations item; definite and arithmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I (c121) deletes and replaces this exact subsection, so the original text has been superseded and its continued presence is at most a housekeeping artefact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain aggregate limit cross-referring to Item 2.c.; nothing to construe in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Superseded by Endorsement 6.I.D (c122), and the Item 2.c. figure ($9,000,000) exceeds the Total Policy Aggregate in Item 4 ($7,000,000), a numerical mismatch the 'subject to' language must absorb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror-image per-condition limit for Coverage B; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleted and replaced by Endorsement 6.I.E (c123), which adds an undefined qualifier ('resulting from covered operations') absent here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror-image aggregate limit for Coverage B; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleted and replaced by Endorsement 6.I.F (c124), again with the undefined 'covered operations' qualifier, so which text controls is not free from doubt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A total-aggregate cap expressed clearly and made 'subject to' the coverage-specific limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 4's $7,000,000 total is smaller than Coverage A's $9,000,000 aggregate in Item 2.c. (c012), so the Declarations and this subsection sit uneasily together even if the cap is meant to control.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'continuous, repeated, or related pollution condition' is an undefined and elastic relatedness test, and 'no other policy shall respond' is a strong deeming provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the single-retention sentence in II.A (c010) and the per-condition limits (c011/c013) without contradicting them, though its reach across prior ACE policies is outside this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard duty-to-defend clause with clearly stated end-points; the 'to which this insurance applies' formula is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II (c125) deletes and replaces this subsection with a three-limb exhaustion test keyed to the dedicated defence sublimit, so the original is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully drafted counsel-selection clause; 'reasonable proximity' and 'similar complexity' are soft but the structure is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F (c128) gives the first named insured the right to select counsel after exhaustion of the defence sublimit, a regime that must be read together with, not against, this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Saying the insured has 'the right and the duty' to retain a consultant while also requiring the insurer's prior written consent is a mild internal pull, though the practical meaning is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4.III (c110) deletes and replaces this very subsection to add catastrophe management firms, so the original text no longer operates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence stating defence costs erode limits and apply to the retention; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleted and replaced by Endorsement 6.II.D (c126), which substitutes the dedicated defence sublimit, so the two texts describe different erosion mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not impose any additional unreasonable burdens' is soft, but the consequence of refusing a recommended settlement is spelled out precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F (c128) restates a garbled version of the same hammer clause for post-exhaustion claims, creating two overlapping settlement regimes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'pollution conditions located ... within the United States' is short and could be tested where a condition migrates across a border, but the intent is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the definition of 'non-owned disposal site' as amended (c133), which is likewise limited to sites within the United States.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines additional insureds by reference to endorsement and limits their rights to those specified; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 2 (c093) names Hoffman Rettig and confines it to vicarious liability, exactly as this definition contemplates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but standard bodily injury definition; 'prospective medical monitoring costs' is delimited by its own purpose clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the Employers Liability exclusion (c056) and the claim definition (c026) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical credential definition requiring mutual agreement; the qualifications language is detailed rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 (c144) excludes all fungi and legionella claims and costs, leaving this definition and the fungi limb of 'remediation costs' (c047) with little or nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'written assertion of a legal right ... including, but not limited to' is an open catch-all with enumerated specifics, the classic setting for a scope argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition is deleted and replaced twice, by Endorsement 8.II (c132) and Endorsement 11.II (c141), each for a different purpose, so which text applies to a given claim needs working out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition of third-party carriage with a defined end point (unloading); little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10.II (c137) deletes Subsection E entirely and substitutes 'transportation', so 'contingent transportation' no longer exists even though exclusion Q in the base form (c069) still refers to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-limb definition dependent on schedules; the numbering is garbled but the content is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both Endorsement 8.I (c131) and Endorsement 11.I (c140) purport to delete and replace this same Subsection F with materially different versions, and Endorsement 11's version refers to a Schedule of Non-Owned Disposal Sites that is not attached.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A hard seventy-two hour window plus an 'imminent and substantial threat' standard; the latter is a familiar regulatory phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It functions as the consent carve-out in III.C (c019/c110) and VII.C (c073/c117) consistently across those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tightly drawn: the obligation must be 'explicitly included' in a contract listed on a schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement is attached to this policy, so the carve-back to the Contractual Liability exclusion (c054) is empty in practice — a coherence point a court could be asked about.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'guidance document' and 'rule' inside a sweeping definition of environmental law give the term unusually elastic edges for a gateway definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It controls the reach of 'remediation costs' (c047) and 'government action' (c035); those provisions depend on it but do not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining the ERP as time to report a claim 'first made against the insured during or subsequent to the end of the policy period' is odd for a claims-made policy that elsewhere requires the claim to be first made during the period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Insuring Agreements A and B (c008/c009), which require the claim to be first made during the policy period, and against VIII.B (c076), which says the ERP does not change the scope of coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assigns premium, retention and agency functions to one identified entity; clear and complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dovetails with 'named insured' (c041), the retention attachment rule (c010) and the ERP conditions (c078/c130) without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but self-referential definition ('byproducts produced or released by fungi'); the circularity is minor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 (c143/c144) removes fungi from 'pollution condition' and excludes fungi claims outright, so this definition survives with no operative field.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward: agency action taken under authority of 'environmental law'; the elasticity comes from the incorporated definition, not this one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the 'claim' definition (c026), which lists government action as an included form of claim.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of irritants closing with 'or waste materials' and 'medical, infectious and pathological wastes' invites an ejusdem generis argument about the catch-all's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is incorporated into 'pollution condition' both in the base form (c045) and as amended by Endorsement 12 (c143), which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition uses 'insured' within its own definition of 'insured' ('employee of ... any insured'), a small circularity, and the trailing scope-of-duties qualifier could be read to attach to more than one antecedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the Insured vs. Insured exclusion (c061) and Separation of Insureds (c085), which speaks only of 'named insureds' though the policy applies to a wider class of 'insureds'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable legal costs, charges, and expenses, including expert charges' is standard; 'reasonable' is a familiar judicial standard rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the erosion provisions (c020, c126) and the dedicated defence sublimit (c127).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical waste classification tracking federal categories; 'greater than specified quantities' leaves the specification unstated but the category is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only inside 'illicit abandonment' (c036) and 'pollution condition' (c045/c143); no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to two named federal statutes as amended; about as determinate as a definition gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the same 'pollution condition' and 'illicit abandonment' provisions without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear cross-reference giving named insureds the same rights except those reserved to the first named insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Subsection K (c033) and with the Separation of Insureds condition (c085), which likewise operates only at the 'named insured' level.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long statutory-style definition; 'other such resources' is a catch-all but is anchored by the preceding enumeration and the trusteeship requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12.III (c145) imposes a $500,000 sublimit on natural resource damage claims, which supplements rather than contradicts this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, broad definition ('any disposal site or recycling facility not owned or operated by an insured') with no qualifiers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.II (c133) deletes and replaces this definition with a far narrower, condition-laden version, so the base text is superseded and the two cannot both operate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 2 is syntactically broken ('the period of time following the closing date ... or, as applicable, through the applicable expiration date'), leaving the start and end of the period for acquired locations unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Automatic Acquisition endorsement is attached, so limb 2 has no field of operation here; limb 1 matches Declarations Items 2.a and 3.a.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant' followed by an illustrative list is the archetypal pollution-definition dispute, and whether a biological agent counts is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12.I (c143) deletes this definition and replaces it with one that drops fungi/legionella and excludes odour, so the base definition's continued relevance (e.g. to 'remediation costs' in c047 and the CIH definition in c025) is unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated limbs including 'diminished value' and 'loss of use'; broad but each limb is defined and bounded to third-party property.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the First-Party Property Damage exclusion (c058), the third-party limitation is reinforced rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to the extent required by environmental law' is the operative constraint and is highly contestable in application, as is 'reasonable expenses'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its fungi/legionella fallback depends on a coverage that Endorsement 12 (c144) excludes altogether, and its 'required by environmental law' trigger leans on the elastic definition in c031.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any employee ... responsible for environmental affairs, control, or compliance' has soft edges but is anchored by the officer/director limb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the Known Conditions (c063), Intentional Non-Compliance (c062) and UST (c068) exclusions, all of which use it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Declarations Items 2.d and 3.d, plus endorsement variation; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 (c108) sets a separate catastrophe-specific retention while c109 refers to 'the self-insured retention' generally, a small overlap the definition's 'or as otherwise designated by endorsement' is meant to absorb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long structured definition of terrorism whose limbs ('to further political, ideological ... objectives') are broad but are standard industry language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the War or Terrorism exclusion (c070); no other provision qualifies it.
